[[File:James Avery Sauls.jpg|thumb|James Avery Sauls]]
'''James Avery Sauls''' is an American physicist.

Sauls studied physics at the [[Colorado School of Mines]], graduating in 1975, and pursued a doctorate in the subject at [[Stony Brook University]], which he completed in 1980. Sauls began his academic career at [[Princeton University]], as research associate, instructor, then assistant professor of physics. In 1987, Sauls joined the faculty of [[Northwestern University]] as associate professor. He became a full professor in 1991.<ref>{{cite news |title=James Avery Sauls - Curriculum Vitae |url=http://eolus.phys.northwestern.edu/cv.html |access-date=21 February 2022 |publisher=Northwestern University |archive-date=21 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220221045024/http://eolus.phys.northwestern.edu/cv.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2021, Sauls was appointed the Sarah Rebecca Roland Professor of Physics.<ref>{{cite news |title=James Sauls Named Sarah Rebecca Roland Professor |url=https://appliedphysics.northwestern.edu/about/news/2021/james-sauls-named-sarah-rebecca-roland-professor.html |access-date=21 February 2022 |publisher=Northwestern University |date=21 July 2021}}</ref>

In 1998, Sauls was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], "[f]or contributions to theories of unconventional superfluidity and superconductivity."<ref>{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=S&year=2021&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=21 February 2022}}</ref> He shared the 2012 {{ill|John Bardeen Prize|de}} with [[Chandra M. Varma]] and [[Steven Kivelson]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2012/05/bardeen-prize/ |last1=Fellman |first1=Megan |title=Physicist Awarded Prestigious John Bardeen Prize |access-date=21 February 2022 |publisher=Northwestern University |date=11 May 2012}} [https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/pt.4.0393/full/ Republished by Physics Today]</ref> In 2017, Sauls was jointly awarded the [[Fritz London Memorial Prize]], sharing the honor with [[William Halperin]] and [[Jeevak Parpia]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fellman |first1=Megan |title=William Halperin and James Sauls are awarded London Prize |url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2017/february/william-halperin-and-james-sauls-are-awarded-london-prize/ |access-date=21 February 2022 |publisher=Northwesern University |date=23 February 2017}}</ref>
